messages:
Maria (partnerships): Quick ask — before we lock the cost model for Q3, I need concrete inputs from HW partners about reserved commit phasing and spot crediting behavior. Specifically: how commits phase over time, proration unit, how spot credits are applied (invoice adjust vs monthly true-up), and eviction/notice windows. Can folks review the CSV sample I sent to partners and flag gaps?

Tom (partner-ops): Agree. Minimal fields we need from partners: commit_start, commit_end, commit_percent (of pool), phasing_profile (linear/step/custom), proration_unit (hour/day), spot_floor_price, crediting_method (invoice_adjust/monthly_trueup), eviction_notice_mins. Also any regional SKU overrides.

Ryan (partner-eng): FYI many infra partners treat credits two ways — immediate negative invoice line-items for the same billing period, or monthly true-ups that net out after usage. Also some partners only credit on reserved SKUs, not ephemeral. We should capture that.

Kate (finance): Please add a column for "latency_premium_flag" and "billing_granularity". We attach latency premiums to SKU prices in the model. If partners return vague language like "prorated", we need the unit (hour/day) to model cost correctly.

Maria (partnerships): Reposting the exact CSV sample I sent — use this when asking partners (ask for one filled row per SKU/region):

```csv
sku_id,region,commit_start,commit_end,commit_percent,phasing_profile,proration_unit,billing_granularity,spot_floor_price,crediting_method,eviction_notice_mins,latency_premium_flag,notes
nebula-gpu-a,us-west-2,2025-07-01,2026-06-30,50,linear,hour,per-hour,0.12,monthly_trueup,30,false,example
voltcloud-rtx,eu-central-1,2025-09-15,2026-03-14,100,step,day,per-day,0.09,invoice_adjust,60,true,commit-cliff at month boundary
```

Alex (vendor-liaison): I'll collect fills from Nebula and VoltCloud. Quick heads-up: Nebula confirmed they do hourly proration and monthly true-ups; VoltCloud said they do day-level proration and invoice-adjust credits. I'll try to get exact example invoices.

Tom (partner-ops): Can we decide on a canonical set of enums so downstream tooling doesn't need fuzzy parsing? Proposed enums: phasing_profile=[linear, step, custom], proration_unit=[hour, day], crediting_method=[invoice_adjust, monthly_trueup, none]. If partner says "custom" attach a short example schedule.

Ryan (partner-eng): Also request eviction handling: are partners giving preempt notice via webhook? If so what's the SLA (mins) and is there any credit when preempt happens < notice window? That affects our fallback routing costs.

Kate (finance): If partners provide only monthly true-ups, we need to model cashflow lag for committed discounts in the forecast. Please mark credit_timing_lag_days if known.

Maria (partnerships): @Alex can you get two completed examples (one hourly-prorate/monthly-trueup, one day-prorate/invoice-adjust) by EOD Wed? Also flag any partners with explicit "commit cliff" or "no pro rata on cancellation" language.

Alex (vendor-liaison): On it — pinging contacts now.

deploy-bot: created shared spreadsheet for partner responses: https://internal.redwood/spreadsheets/PartnerCommitInputs (permissions: partnerships + finance) :spiral_calendar:

Tom (partner-ops): If any partner won't give exact numbers, default assumptions for modeling: commit_percent fallback = 100% of reserved pool, proration_unit = day, crediting_method = monthly_trueup, eviction_notice_mins = 0. Call these "conservative defaults" and tag in the model.

Maria (partnerships): Perfect. We'll use conservative defaults until we get concrete fills. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
